6C. GENERAL PLAN AMENDMENT NO. 24-00002 (GPA24-00002) AINS: 4030-
033-901, 4030-033-903, AND 4030-033-904: A public hearing to
consider an application by Megan Divine, representing HAS INWD
Property Owner, LLC, for General Plan Amendment No. 24-00002 (GPA24-
00002) to allow a request to amend the Land Use Element Map of the
Inglewood General Plan from Low Density to Medium Density for an
approximately 68-acre site (Morningside High school and Monroe
Middle school) with approximately 22.87 acres designated for a
proposed multiple-family residential development at (AINs: 4030-033-
901, 4030-033-903, and 4030-033-904).

Mr. McCrumby stated he would like to make a few points of
clarification at the beginning of said presentation:
1. This application came in prior to the commencement of our
Comprehensive General Plan Update, which is why we need to move
forward with it as it came from the applicant’s request. Any future
developments outside of the 22-acres that were analyzed in the SCEA
would require its own environmental analysis. Any project that
happens outside the proposed future development, should this GPA be
recommended to City Council for approval would require its own
environmental analysis.
2. A programmatic EIR is going to be conducted, Citywide that would
also look at the future development capacity for any land use changes
that are made by way of the General Plan Amendment and our
Comprehensive General Plan Update.
3. The school sites are remaining as they currently are. Morningside
High School and Monroe Middle School is an active school campus.
There are no development plans for anything to happen on those sites.

Mr. Angel Leon-Martell, Planner, made the staff presentation.

DISCUSSION
The Inglewood Municipal Code (IMC), Chapter 12, Articles 10.7 and 25, requires approval
of a Special Use Permit (SUP) to allow the expansion of an existing single-tenant fast-
food restaurant and restaurant.

The applicant requests Special Use Permit approval for the following:

Manchester Boulevard and Locust Street and is zoned H-C (Historic Core). The site is
developed with a free-standing fast-food restaurant and a detached one-story, multiple-
tenant commercial building. Surrounding land uses to the north and east are zoned R-4
and C-2 with multiple-family residential uses and a gas station. The properties to the south
and west are zoned H-C and developed with commercial uses.

Site Design
The existing site currently features a single drive-through lane serving the fast-food
restaurant. The proposed improvements aim to enhance traffic flow and customer service
efficiency by introducing an additional lane. As part of the proposed work, the project will
include the installation of two (2) digital menu boards, two (2) preview boards, concrete
curbs, protective bollards, and a clearance bar structure. These additions are designed
to improve operational capacity and safety within the drive-through area.

to extend the drive-through lane and accommodate an additional vehicle. The applicant
also proposes to relocate an existing trash enclosure, currently situated at the northeast

restaurant. The new enclosure will be constructed with a six-foot concrete masonry wall
finished with cement plaster and will include a six-foot galvanized steel gate. The gate will
be painted to match the existing building, ensuring visual consistency with the overall site
design. The applicant proposes a planting palette consisting of star jasmine, pink dancer,

BACKGROUND
On May 14, 1970, the Building Safety Division issued a Certificate of Occupancy for a
2,540 square-foot service station.

On November 3, 1999, Special Use Permit No. 847 (SP-847) was partially approved to
allow the conversion of an auto repair building into a 2,540 square-foot convenience
market. The SUP also included a request to allow the off-site sale of beer and wine at the
subject site. The Planning Commission denied the request due to the crime rate in the
Census Tract being more than twice the City’s average, as well as an over-concentration
of existing alcohol licenses in the area, which significantly exceeds the threshold set by
the State Alcoholic Beverage Control (ABC) Board.

On March 6, 2002, the Planning Commission approved Special Use Permit No. 913 (SP-
913) to allow a 115 square-foot addition to the convenience market.

On October 7, 2009, the Planning Commission denied Special Use Permit No.1098 (SP-
1098) to allow the sale of beer and wine for off-site consumption for the existing service
station. The Planning Commission denied the request based on three (3) key factors: the
over concentration of existing off-sale beer and wine liceneses in the census tract, the
proximity of the proposed site to a church and playground (within 600 feet), and the fact
that the location falls within a high-crime reporting district with crime rates exceeding the
city average.

On October 22, 2009, the Planning Division received an appeal letter and fee from the
applicant.

On December 8, 2009, the City Council denied the applicants appeal for SP-1098.

In September 2024, Veers Legacy Partners Inc. filed for a business license for a change
of ownership. The current business operates as a service station with a convenience
market.

On August 5, 2025, the Planning Commission continued the Public Hearing to the next
available Planning Commission meeting at the request of the applicant.

The Inglewood Municipal Code (IMC), Chapter 12, Articles 10.6 and 25, requires approval
of a Special Use Permit (SUP) to allow the sale of beer and wine for off-site consumption.

The applicant is requesting approval of a Special Use Permit to allow:
  1. The sale of beer and wine for off-site consumption.

Avenue. The property is zoned MU-C (Mixed Use Corridor). The properties to the west,
